{{rfq|en}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|translatioun||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:translacioun|tree=1}}

From {{inh|en|enm|translacioun|t=transfer, translation}}, from {{der|en|xno|translacioun}}, from {{der|en|la|trānslātiō}}, from {{m|la||trānslāt-}}, the {{lg|supine}} stem of {{m|la|trānsferō|t=to transfer, transport, transform, translate}}. {{surf|en|translate|-ion}}. {{displaced|ang|wending}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/tɹænzˈleɪʃən/|/tɹæns-/|/tɹɑːnz-/|/tɹɑːns-/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/tɹænzˈleɪʃən/|/tɹæns-/|a=GA}}

* {{audio|en|En-us-translation.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪʃən|s=3}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~|abbr=tr.,trans.,transl.}}

# {{lb|en|countable|uncountable}} The [[act]] of [[translate|translating]].
## The [[conversion]] of [[text]] from one [[language]] to another.
##: {{ux|en|This old text needs '''translation''' into modern English before it is published.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2020-02-10|journal=w:San Francisco Chronicle|title=Original or translated? Great literature takes both forms|author=Barbara Lane|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/entertainment/books/article/original-or-translated-great-literature-takes-21177692.php
|text=In the United States, she says, only 3% of the books published are in '''translation''' from another language.}}
## {{lb|en|translation studies}} The [[discipline]] or study of translating written language (as opposed to [[interpretation]], which concerns itself with spoken language).
## The [[conversion]] of something from one [[form]] or [[medium]] to another.
## {{lb|en|physics|mathematics}} A [[motion]] or [[compulsion]] to [[motion]] in a [[straight line]] without [[rotation]] or other [[deformation]].
## {{lb|en|mathematics}} A [[relation]] between two [[mathematical]] [[figure]]s such as a [[straight line]] where the coordinates of each [[point]] in one [[figure]] is a constant added to the [[coordinates]] of a corresponding point in the other figure.
## {{lb|en|genetics}} The [[process]] whereby a [[strand]] of [[mRNA]] [[direct]]s [[assembly]] of [[amino acid]]s into [[protein]]s within a [[ribosome]].
## {{lb|en|physics}} A [[transfer]] of [[motion]] [[occur]]ring within a [[gearbox]].
## The [[automatic]] [[retransmission]] of a [[telegraph]] [[message]].
## The [[conveyance]] of something from one [[place]] to another, [[especially]]:
### {{lb|en|Christianity}} An [[ascension]] to [[Heaven]] without [[death]].
### {{lb|en|Christianity}} A [[transfer]] of a [[bishop]] from one [[diocese]] to another.
### {{lb|en|Christianity}} A [[transfer]] of a [[holy]] [[relic]] from one [[shrine]] to another.
### {{lb|en|medicine}} A [[transfer]] of a [[disease]] from one [[body part]] to another.
# {{lb|en|countable}} The [[product]] or [[end result]] of an [[act]] of [[translate|translating]].
